subject: FinPay - follow-up: competitive TCO and next tests
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: FinPay - follow-up: competitive TCO and next tests

Hi Ben / Naomi —

Thanks again for taking the run-through today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Call highlights
- Goals: reduce inference unit cost for chat and summarize flows, target 2–3x improvement vs your current endpoint spend while keeping 100–200ms P95 generation latency for 1–2k token responses.
- Current baseline: you mentioned ~80M tokens/month for batching-heavy summary jobs and ~15M tokens/month for low-latency chat.
- Key constraints: PCI scope, regional residency (US), and <200ms P95 for chat.

What Redwood can help validate next
1) Cost/TCO comparison vs your current hyperscaler endpoint (we'll model per-1M tokens): batching + cache vs single-request baseline
2) Latency impact of batching and KV cache hit rates — measure P50/P95 for both chat and summarize flows
3) A short pilot with identical prompts to compare quality and failure modes

Immediate next steps (proposed)
- I attached a short TCO workbook (redwood_finpay_tco_q3_v1.xlsx) with an initial per-1M token calc and assumptions. Please review and flag anything off.
- If you’re good, we’ll run two tests next week: a) 1M token synthetic run to validate per-1M unit cost at your typical batch sizes, and b) 5k chat requests to capture P95 latency and cold-start behavior.
- Marcus will own test orchestration and will reach out to align on keys and VPC access.

Open questions for you (short)
- Exact batch sizes you use for summary jobs (avg tokens/request and average batch size)
- Current cache hit % if you use a prefix/KV cache today

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 15 if you want to finalize the test plan.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124

From: Ben Lewis <ben.lewis@finpay.com>

Date: 2026-08-02T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinPay - follow-up: competitive TCO and next tests

Aditya —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick answers:
- Batch sizes: summary jobs are usually 16–32 requests per batch; average payload ~600 tokens; so roughly 9–12k tokens per batch depending on how we chunk.
- Cache: we don't have a dedicated KV cache in front of the model today; we do application-level memoization for a small % (maybe 6–8% effective reuse).
- Latency: our target is <200ms P95 for chat (we're seeing ~250–300ms P95 today on peak).

We reviewed the attached workbook at a high level — looks reasonable. Two asks before we run tests:
1) Can you show a head-to-head per-1M tokens estimate comparing Redwood hosted API vs our current AWS Sagemaker endpoint (including expected impact of batching and a 30% cache-hit scenario)?
2) Can Marcus run a small synthetic run with the same prompt set we used today so we can compare latency numbers apples-to-apples?

We can do the pilot next Wed/Thu. If that works, Naomi (copied) will share keys and a short sample dataset.

Ben
Director of Engineering, FinPay
ben.lewis@finpay.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Ben Lewis <ben.lewis@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinPay - follow-up: competitive TCO and next tests

Ben / Naomi —

Great — thanks for the details. Summary of what we'll deliver prior to the pilot:

1) Per-1M token TCO comparison (Redwood hosted API vs AWS Sagemaker endpoint) — assumptions we used in the workbook:
- Token definition: 1 token ≈ 4 characters; 1M tokens used as normalization point.
- Baseline (your current Sagemaker endpoint): we modeled your observed latency profile and the lack of an integrated KV cache. We included endpoint vCPU/GPU amortized costs, network egress (estim), and orchestration overhead.
- Redwood model: we modeled batching at your reported sizes (16–32) and two cache scenarios (0% and 30% effective hit). We also include Redwood's prefix/KV caching and continuous batching benefits.

Key headline numbers (per-1M tokens) — rough estimates, see workbook for itemized line items:
- Current Sagemaker endpoint (no cache): ~$1,100 per 1M tokens (chat-like workloads, low batching);
- Redwood hosted (batching 16–32, cache 0%): ~$650 per 1M tokens;
- Redwood hosted (batching 16–32, cache 30%): ~$480 per 1M tokens;

Notes on sensitivities:
- Batch size: increasing average batch size from 16 -> 32 lowers per-1M by ~15–20% (depends on avg token/request).
- Cache hit rate: each 10% of cache hit reduces active token cost ~6–8% in our model because served tokens are skipped and KV hits avoid decoder steps.
- Latency: for chat flows with 1–2k token responses, we can keep P95 <200ms with a 16–24 batching strategy plus warm KV cache and model variant optimized for latency (e.g., redwood-alpha-legalv1 -> quantized low-latency variant).

Suggested pilot tests (we'll run both in parallel):
A) Synthetic per-1M token run (2–4 hr): generate 1M tokens at your average payload and batching settings to validate per-token unit economics.
B) Chat latency run (15–30 minutes): replay 5k chat requests at your target concurrency to capture P50/P95 and tail behavior.

Logistics: Marcus will coordinate keys and compute. Notes: for accurate cache-hit modeling, please include a representative set of prior prompts/responses so we can seed the KV. If you can't share content, synthetic repeats are OK to approximate reuse.

Marcus — can you confirm availability for Wed/Thu next week and the minimal access you need? I'll also upload an updated workbook with the detailed line items to the Drive link and attach the file here.

Best,
Aditya

Ben / Naomi —

I'm available Wed/Thu next week — Wed 10:00–13:00 PT or Thu 09:00–11:00 PT work for me. For the synthetic runs I'll need:
- API key for a test environment (can be time-limited) OR a short-lived SSH access to a staging VPC if you want Private deployment tests
